oauth.alternatives: In your own workspace, you can use the bot token from your install. Other workspaces each need their own OAuth install.

appTypes.name: Internal app (your own workspace only)
appTypes.whenToUse: Prototyping, or a customer building in their own workspace. Normal conversations.history limits (50+ requests a minute, up to 1,000 messages per call).

appTypes.name: Unlisted distributed app (public distribution, not in the Marketplace)
appTypes.whenToUse: Pilots. Any workspace can install it without review. New installs get conversations.history and conversations.replies once a minute, 15 messages per call.

appTypes.name: Slack Marketplace app
appTypes.whenToUse: Commercial scale. Needs 10 active workspaces to submit, then about 12 weeks of review. Restores normal history limits.

appTypes.name: Org-ready app (Enterprise orgs)
appTypes.whenToUse: Enterprise Grid customers wanting one install across workspaces. Opt in to org-level apps; an Org Admin approves.

verdict.label: Self-serve, optional review
verdict.summary: Any workspace can install your app without review. The deciding factor is the read limit: unlisted apps read history once a minute, 15 messages per call. Production needs a Marketplace listing.
verdict.nextStep: Create an app at api.slack.com/apps, install it, and read through message events.
verdict.customerSideGateNote: Workspace owners can require app approval, so members can only request your app. On Enterprise Grid, org policy can require approval per workspace, and org-wide installs need an Org Admin.

composio.note: Composio provides managed OAuth for Slack and a separate Slackbot toolkit. Users see Composio on the install screen, and you share its quota. Bring your own app for your own name, scopes, or rate limits. Only new connections use it. Existing users stay on the old one until they reconnect or you import their credentials. Ask Composio whether its app is Marketplace-listed, since that sets your history limit.

stages.name: Prototype
stages.notes: Internal apps keep normal history limits. Test summarization here. Use a free developer sandbox for paid-plan features like the agent container.

stages.name: Limited beta
stages.whoCanConnect: Any workspace via your install link, unless admins require approval.
stages.notes: No Slack review. You wait only on customer admins who require approval. Slack intends unlisted distribution for pilots.

stages.name: Production
stages.whoCanConnect: Any workspace, from the Marketplace, with normal history limits.
stages.notes: You need 10 active workspaces through the whole review. Slack states up to 10 business days for preliminary feedback and up to 10 weeks for functional review. Resubmitting during preliminary review resets your queue place. No verified developer reports exist.

scopeTiers.name: Reply and post as a bot
scopeTiers.effect: Any workspace, no review. Reply to mentions and DMs via events. Tokens do not expire unless rotation is on.

scopeTiers.name: Read channels in real time (events)
scopeTiers.effect: No review while unlisted. Message events arrive live from channels the bot is in. Fetching older threads still hits the 1 per minute limit.

scopeTiers.name: Read history on demand at full speed
scopeTiers.effect: Full limits only for internal and Marketplace apps. A Marketplace listing puts *:history scopes under enhanced review.

scopeTiers.name: Search and admin
scopeTiers.effect: Restricted scopes. Marketplace generally rejects them, and admin.* rarely passes outside Slack's partner program. Use the Real-time Search API for search.

requirements.item: A Slack workspace where you can install apps
requirements.detail: Sign-in required. A free developer sandbox works if your workspace limits installs.
redirect_uri must use HTTPS, match or sit under a configured Redirect URL, and contain no #. Send the same value in both authorize and token steps.

requirements.item: An OAuth install flow, not a hard-coded token
requirements.detail: Each workspace gets its own token from oauth.v2.access. Store tokens per workspace and user.
Events API, interactivity, slash commands, and options load URLs need SSL to distribute.

requirements.item: Reads that survive 1 request a minute
requirements.detail: Read new messages from events. Queue history fetches.
Active means used in the last 28 days, not a sandbox. Stay at 10 or more through review.

requirements.item: Public landing page, privacy policy, and support page
requirements.detail: The privacy policy covers collection, use, retention, and deletion requests via email or form. Support must answer within 2 business days.
Request only scopes for existing features. *:history scopes get enhanced review.

requirements.item: AI disclosures, no training on Slack data
requirements.detail: Disclose model, retention, data tenancy, and data residency, and warn that output can be wrong. Never train on Slack data. Agent apps store metadata only and fetch data when needed.
Name, short description of 10 words or fewer, long description, icon, 1600x1000 screenshots under 2MB, and a recommended 30 to 90 second video.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: At api.slack.com/apps, click **Create New App**. Choose **From scratch** or **From a manifest** and pick your workspace. **Basic Information** shows the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Add scopes and redirect URL
steps.detail: Under **OAuth & Permissions**, add bot scopes such as `chat:write`, `app_mentions:read`, and `channels:history`, and your HTTPS redirect URL. Mark nice-to-have scopes optional.

steps.title: Turn on Agents if needed
steps.detail: For the split-view agent container, turn on **Agents** and add `assistant:write`. Some AI features need a paid plan, so test in a free sandbox and confirm free plans still work.

steps.title: Subscribe to message events
steps.detail: Under **Event Subscriptions**, set an HTTPS request URL and subscribe to `app_mention`, `message.im`, and `message.channels`.

steps.title: Install and test
steps.detail: Install the app, invite the bot to a test channel, and summarize a thread.

steps.title: Build the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Redirect to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with client ID, scopes, state, and redirect_uri. Verify state, exchange the code with oauth.v2.access within 10 minutes, and store the token by team or enterprise ID.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation
steps.detail: Rotation gives 12-hour access tokens and single-use refresh tokens, and cannot be turned off. Without it, tokens do not expire. Confirm Composio or your broker handles rotation first.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: In **Manage Distribution**, complete the checklist and click **Activate Public Distribution**. You get an **Add to Slack** button and install link.

steps.title: Opt in to org-level installs
steps.detail: For Enterprise Grid, add a bot scope like `team:read`, choose **Opt-In** under **Org Level Apps**, and handle is_enterprise_install. An Org Admin installs and picks workspaces.

steps.title: Send pilots the admin note
steps.detail: App approval is off by default but common at large companies and on Enterprise Grid. Send each pilot's workspace owner the admin note draft.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspaces
steps.detail: Keep 10 non-sandbox workspaces active in the last 28 days, through the whole review.

steps.title: Submit the listing
steps.detail: Publish landing, privacy, and support pages. In **Submit to the Slack Marketplace**, pass automated checks and add the listing, scope reasons, test account, and a demo video of install, use, and uninstall.

steps.title: Wait for review
steps.detail: Slack checks the listing, then a reviewer tests the app. Answer all feedback. Slack does not expedite for launch dates.
steps.estimate: Up to about 12 weeks, as Slack states

blockers.symptom: conversations.history returns 15 messages and rate limits after one call a minute.
blockers.cause: Distributed apps outside the Marketplace get the reduced limit on new installs.
blockers.fix: Read from events, queue history fetches, and get Marketplace approval for full speed.
blockers.escalation: Ask Slack developer support if your app counts as commercially distributed.

blockers.symptom: Members can only request the app.
blockers.fix: Send the workspace owner the admin note draft with your scope list.

blockers.cause: redirect_uri differs between authorize and oauth.v2.access, or is not under a configured Redirect URL.
blockers.fix: Send the same HTTPS redirect_uri in both and add it under **OAuth & Permissions**.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace submission is blocked or returned early.
blockers.cause: Fewer than 10 active workspaces, before or during review.
blockers.fix: Grow non-sandbox installs active in the last 28 days.

blockers.cause: History scopes get enhanced review, and broad access without a clear use rarely passes.
blockers.fix: Limit history to channels the bot is in, and explain and demo the exact feature.

blockers.symptom: The app stops working after a person leaves.
blockers.cause: Apps with scopes beyond bot, commands, webhooks, or identify are uninstalled when the installer leaves or becomes a guest.
blockers.fix: Handle app_uninstalled and prompt reinstall; prefer bot scopes.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails, or tokens stop after 12 hours.
blockers.cause: Rotation is on and you reused a refresh token, which works once after a short grace period.
blockers.fix: Store the newest refresh token from every refresh.

blockers.cause: Some scopes are not allowed on org-level installs.
blockers.fix: Remove the scope or use a workspace-level install.

didForYou: Read about 21 official Slack and Composio pages and the changelog, and cited each claim.
Probed slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with an invalid client ID. It returns 200 with a script redirect.
Checked api.slack.com/apps. It loads and requires sign-in.
Drafted a channels:history reason, admin note, app description, and privacy checklist.
canDoForYou: Write a manifest with scopes, events, redirect URL, and agent settings.
Write the OAuth flow, state check, token storage, and rotation.
Build an events-first reader and rate-limited history queue.
Draft listing copy, scope reasons, AI disclosures, and demo script.
Fill app settings in a browser after you sign in.
youMustDo: Sign in to Slack and create the app.
Decide on token rotation, which is permanent.
Get pilot customers and admins to install and approve.
Publish a privacy policy and support page.
Record the demo video and submit to the Marketplace.
Accept Slack's API terms, including no model training on Slack data.

drafts.title: channels:history scope reason
drafts.body:
DRAFT, edit before use.

Scope: channels:history (bot token)

[App name] summarizes threads and drafts replies in Slack. When a user mentions @[App name] in a thread or clicks Summarize thread, we call conversations.replies for that thread and post a summary.

We read only public channels the bot was added to. We do not bulk read or export history.

We store only channel and thread IDs, not message text. Text goes to [model provider] only to summarize and is not used for training.

Without this scope, thread summaries do not work.

To test: install the app, invite @[App name] to a channel, start a thread, then mention @[App name] summarize.

drafts.title: Workspace admin approval note
drafts.body:
DRAFT, edit before use.

Hi [admin name],

I requested approval for [App name]. It summarizes threads and drafts replies when mentioned.

Access:
- Public channel messages, only where the bot is added (channels:history)
- Mentions and direct messages to the app (app_mentions:read, im:history)
- Posting replies as the bot (chat:write)

It does not read other channels or export messages, and the vendor states it does not train AI models on our data. Privacy policy: [URL]. Security: [URL].

Approve it under Admin, Apps and workflows, App management settings. You can remove it there any time.

Thanks,
[Your name]

drafts.title: Marketplace descriptions
drafts.body:
DRAFT, edit before use.

Short (10 words or fewer): Summarize Slack threads and draft replies with AI.

Long: Mention @[App name] in a thread to get a summary of decisions and open questions, or a draft reply you can edit.

Add the bot to the channels you want. It reads only those, and only when asked.

AI notice: [model] generates summaries, which can be wrong. Slack data is not stored after the summary and never trains models.

drafts.title: Privacy policy checklist
drafts.body:
DRAFT, edit before use.

- Slack data collected (message text, user IDs, channel IDs).
- How you use it.
- Retention. If you keep nothing, say so.
- Data received but unused.
- How users or admins request access, transfer, or deletion.
- A contact email or web form.
- The AI model, where it runs, and provider retention.
- No training on Slack data.
- A public support page, no account needed, replies within 2 business days.

uncertainties.question: Do reduced history limits now apply to installs before May 29, 2025?
uncertainties.why: Slack says existing installs are unaffected with no end date, while unsourced reports cite March 3, 2026 or September 2, 2025.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Ask Slack developer support, or test limits on an old unlisted install.

uncertainties.question: Does the 1 per minute limit apply to user tokens too?
uncertainties.why: The changelog describes the limit per app, not per token type.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Ask Slack developer support, or test both token types.

uncertainties.question: How long does Marketplace review take in practice?
uncertainties.why: No developer report confirms Slack's stated timeline, and the submission page shows its estimate only after sign-in.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Read your submission page estimate, or ask other Slack partners.

uncertainties.question: Is Composio's managed Slack app Marketplace-listed?
uncertainties.why: If not, managed connections get reduced history limits, and Composio's docs do not say.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Ask Composio support, or search the Slack Marketplace.

uncertainties.question: Does a free pilot count as commercial distribution?
uncertainties.why: Slack ties the rate limit to commercial distribution but does not define where free or trial use falls.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Ask Slack developer support before a large unlisted rollout.

evidence.claim: Slack uses OAuth v2 at slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize. The redirect_uri must be HTTPS, match or sit under a configured Redirect URL, and match between steps or you get bad_redirect_uri. Codes expire after 10 minutes. Tokens do not expire unless rotation is on. Some scopes fail org installs with scope_not_allowed_on_enterprise.

After you activate public distribution, any workspace can install the app unless it limits installs to admins, to Marketplace apps, or requires admin approval. Redirect, events, and interactivity URLs need SSL. Unlisted distribution is meant for pilots and early customers.
Apps with scopes other than bot, incoming-webhook, commands, or identify are uninstalled when the installing user leaves the workspace or becomes a guest.

From May 29, 2025, new unlisted apps and new installs of existing unlisted apps can call conversations.history and conversations.replies 1 time a minute with a limit of 15 objects. Marketplace apps are not affected. Internal customer-built apps keep 50+ a minute and 1,000 objects.
evidence.sourceTitle: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps

evidence.claim: Slack's changelog says the new limits are not applied to existing installations of unlisted apps.
evidence.sourceTitle: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps

evidence.claim: The updated API terms name the Slack Marketplace as the only appropriate channel for commercially distributing apps, including unlisted ones. Slack says the history limit is meant to stop bulk data exfiltration by unvetted apps.
evidence.sourceTitle: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps (FAQ)

evidence.claim: Marketplace apps with fewer than 10 active workspaces and fewer than 10 weekly active users are unsuitable. *:history, files:read, search:read.* and admin.* scopes get enhanced review. Restricted scopes such as search:read and admin.* are generally rejected.
evidence.sourceTitle: Slack Marketplace app guidelines and requirements

evidence.claim: Marketplace AI apps must not train models on Slack data, must disclose the model, data retention, tenancy, and residency, must warn about inaccurate output, and agent container apps must disclose the paid plan need. Agent apps may not store Slack data they obtain.
evidence.sourceTitle: Slack Marketplace app guidelines and requirements

evidence.claim: Listings need a short description of 10 words or fewer, 1600x1000 images under 2MB, a public landing page, a privacy policy covering collection, use, retention, and deletion, and support that answers within 2 business days.
evidence.sourceTitle: Slack Marketplace app guidelines and requirements

evidence.claim: Preliminary review feedback takes up to 10 business days and functional review up to 10 weeks for new apps (6 weeks for updates). Resubmitting in the preliminary stage resets your queue place. Slack does not expedite for launch dates.
Reviewers install the app in their own workspace, test install, OAuth, use, and uninstall, and check a reason for each scope. A demo video is recommended.
As of July 2026, Marketplace submissions need at least 10 installs on active workspaces, up from a temporary lower threshold, and must stay at 10 or more for the whole review.
evidence.sourceTitle: Updated installation requirement for Slack Marketplace apps

evidence.claim: Slack's API terms (effective 10 October 2025) bar using API data to train a large language model and bar bulk export without a separate agreement.
evidence.note: The terms also bar persistent copies and indexes of other organizations' data for the Data Access and Real-time Search APIs.

evidence.claim: With token rotation, access tokens last 12 hours and each refresh token works once. Rotation cannot be turned off once on. Without rotation, access tokens never expire.
PKCE became generally available on March 30, 2026. Enabling it marks the app as a public client and cannot be undone without support. Refresh tokens for PKCE apps expire after 30 days.

Workspace owners can require approved apps under App management settings. Members then request apps and owners or app managers approve them. On Enterprise Grid, an org app management policy turns on approval for the workspace.
evidence.sourceTitle: Manage app approval for your workspace

evidence.claim: To support org-wide installs you add a bot scope, opt in under Org Level Apps (org_deploy_enabled), and an Org Admin approves and installs the app, then chooses workspaces.
assistant:write is a bot scope that lets the app act as an AI assistant app and call assistant.threads.setStatus, setSuggestedPrompts, and setTitle.
channels:history lets the app view messages in public channels it has been added to. It covers conversations.history, conversations.replies, and message events such as message.channels.
Slack rate limit tiers are per method, per workspace, per app: Tier 1 is 1+ a minute and Tier 3 is 50+ a minute.
Composio lists Slack and Slackbot under Composio-managed OAuth available.

Existing connected accounts stay on the auth config they were created with. Only new connections use your custom config. To move existing users, they reconnect or you import their credentials where supported.
Reasons to bring your own app include your own name on the consent screen, custom scopes, a dedicated rate limit quota, and faster polling than the 15 minute managed minimum.
The authorization endpoint slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize is live.
evidence.note: GET with an invalid client ID returned HTTP 200 and a small page whose script redirects to the same URL with tracked=1. We did not follow it, so we did not see the error shown for an unknown client.

evidence.claim: Developer portal api.slack.com/apps loads and asks you to sign in to your Slack account to create an app.
evidence.note: HTTP 200, page title Slack API: Applications.

evidence.claim: On February 17, 2026 Slack released an MCP server and the Real-time Search API, which grew out of the Data Access API and lets apps fetch relevant Slack data without storing it.
evidence.sourceTitle: Announcing the Slack MCP server and Real-time Search API
evidence.note: Read from the changelog index page at docs.slack.dev/changelog.

evidence.claim: A community article says the grace period for existing unlisted installs ended March 3, 2026. It links no Slack source and conflicts with Slack's changelog.
evidence.sourceTitle: Slack just throttled your OpenClaw agent

evidence.claim: An agent that reads threads on demand across many customer workspaces needs a Marketplace listing to work well in production.
evidence.note: At 1 call a minute and 15 messages per call, catching up on a busy channel takes many minutes per workspace. Only Marketplace and internal apps get normal limits, and Slack's terms point commercial apps to the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Since March 16, 2026 you can mark individual OAuth scopes as optional, so users can install without granting them.
evidence.note: Read from the changelog index page at docs.slack.dev/changelog.

evidence.claim: An unlisted app can read new messages through Events API message events without calling conversations.history, so the reduced limit mostly hurts backfill and on-demand thread reads.
evidence.note: The rate limit change names only conversations.history and conversations.replies. channels:history also grants message events. Not tested, and Marketplace AI rules still discourage storing message data.

evidence.claim: A news report says Slack capped conversations.history and conversations.replies at 1 request a minute and 15 messages for apps not in the Marketplace, starting May 29, 2025 for new apps and new installs. Marketplace apps keep normal limits.
evidence.sourceTitle: Slack adds a 1 per minute limit to some APIs for non-Marketplace apps (Japanese)
evidence.note: Independent second source for the history limit. It also says existing installs would be limited from September 2, 2025, which Slack's changelog no longer says.

evidence.claim: Activating public distribution gives you an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL. Many users will need admin approval before they can install your app.
evidence.sourceTitle: Get to know the Slack app types (Trailhead)
evidence.note: Second source for self-serve distribution. It does not mention any Slack review step for distributed apps.

evidence.claim: After you create an agent app, app settings show an Agents feature in the sidebar and the assistant:write scope. Some AI features need a paid plan, and a free Developer Program sandbox has them.
Apps must be installed on 10 or more active workspaces, used in the past 28 days, or they are blocked from submitting to the Marketplace.

changelog.change: Added a news report (e32) and a Salesforce Trailhead page (e33) as second sources for the history limit and for self-serve public distribution.
changelog.reason: Tier-deciding claims need a second independent source. Both match Slack's own pages.

changelog.change: Step s13 estimate changed from 2 to 12 weeks to up to about 12 weeks.
changelog.reason: Slack states only upper limits: up to 10 business days, then up to 10 weeks. It gives no 2 week minimum.

changelog.change: Requirement r9 and evidence e8 now say agent apps must not store Slack data, and list data tenancy as a disclosure.
changelog.reason: The guidelines say agent apps may not store Slack data, which is stronger than should not.

changelog.change: Step s8 no longer lists removing hard-coded tokens as a checklist item.
changelog.reason: The distribution page names OAuth and SSL as preparation. It does not mention hard-coded tokens.

changelog.change: Step s3 now names the Agents feature and asks you to check that assistant:write is present.
changelog.reason: The assistant:write scope page does not say the feature adds the scope. Slack's agent docs now call the sidebar feature Agents and list the scope with it.

changelog.change: Step s10 changed from many workspaces require approval to some workspaces do, and notes it is off by default.
changelog.reason: Slack's help article says members can install apps without approval by default. How common approval is, is not stated.

changelog.change: Token rotation blocker no longer names invalid_refresh_token as the error.
changelog.reason: The token rotation page says reusing a refresh token fails but names no error code.

changelog.change: Composio note now mentions credential import as a second way to move existing users.
changelog.reason: Composio's white-labeling page offers re-authentication or credential import.

changelog.change: Uncertainty about older installs now lists a second conflicting date (September 2, 2025) from a news report.
changelog.reason: Two third-party sources give different end dates for the grace period. Slack's current changelog gives none.
